name: Ana Roxanne
label: Kranky
lede: Ana Roxanne Recto wanted to be Alicia Keys, then studied jazz in Iowa and Hindustani singing in India before landing at Mills College with a room of analog synthesizers. Six years after her Kranky debut, she took the tape haze off her voice.

eras.title: From Vallejo to Iowa, India and Oakland
eras.text: Ana Roxanne Recto grew up in Vallejo on R&B, oldies and Catholic choir, then spent her twenties chasing voices: Iowa jazz, a Minneapolis math-rock band, a teacher in northern India. Each stop gave her a different way to use one instrument.

q: Deerhoof were a part of my gateway into the world of experimental music.
years.h: A Vallejo kid heads to Iowa to study jazz voice
years.p: Homeschooled, then Catholic-schooled in a Filipino community, Ana Roxanne Recto moved to Iowa in 2005 for jazz and classical study at a community college. She sang choral music in Midwest cathedrals, dropped out of the jazz program, finished college, and spent three years in a progressive/math-rock band in Minneapolis.
years.xp:
Her father played classical music and oldies at home and her mother played R&B, according to Wikipedia. Watching Alicia Keys on MTV is what made her want to sing.

Years later she told The Quietus she was "a fresh drop-out out of jazz school" when she found experimental music, and named Deerhoof's Apple O' as a gateway.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ana Roxanne · ICA: In the Round
years.h: She flies to Uttarakhand to learn Hindustani singing
years.p: Wikipedia describes the 2013 trip as changing how she understood singing itself. She went to study traditional Hindustani vocal technique.

years.h: Mills College puts analog synths in front of her
years.p: Back from India, she enrolled at Mills, the Oakland school known for its electronic music program, and started working with analog synthesizers.

eras.title: A private EP, then everyone hears it
eras.text: The record that made her name sat unreleased for years. She made it in the Bay Area, kept it among friends, then let Matthewdavid's Leaving Records put it out as she began speaking publicly about being intersex.

years.h: Six tracks she plays only for friends
years.p: She finished the music that became the ~~~ EP in 2015 and shared it privately, unsure how such an intimate record would land.
years.xp: Resident Advisor reported that fear as the reason it stayed unannounced.

years.big: "It feels like I was always singing in code with these songs."
q: It feels like I was always singing in code with these songs.
years.src: Resident Advisor · The Vinyl Factory · Wikipedia: Because of a Flower
years.h: She comes out as intersex, and her EP changes meaning
years.p: Ana Roxanne began speaking publicly about being intersex in October 2018, months before ~~~ got a proper release. She was talking to Resident Advisor about the EP.
years.xp:
Resident Advisor tied the two together: the EP, made in 2015, carried an identity she had not yet said out loud. The Vinyl Factory reported that the cassette release coincided with her going public.

The subject runs through her later work. Because of a Flower takes its title from it.

years.cap: Ana Roxanne in her studio, around the release of ~~~, 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Tilde Tilde Tilde · Resident Advisor · The Vinyl Factory
years.p: Six tracks: field recordings, a Moog IIIP, hushed vocals and a cover of "I'm Every Sparkly Woman". Matthewdavid mastered it and released it on his Leaving Records imprint.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 7.3, with Anna Gaca calling it "restful and restorative". The Quietus's Jo Higgs praised the synth and organ under sparse vocal melodies and field recordings, according to Wikipedia.

Wikipedia's infobox lists March 19, 2015 as the release date. Resident Advisor and The Vinyl Factory place the label release in 2019.

years.h: Vinyl for ~~~, after a spring of Los Angeles shows
years.p: The Vinyl Factory announced the LP edition in July 2019, after the cassette had run earlier that year.

eras.title: Kranky signs her, and a duet follows
eras.text: Kranky gave her a first full-length. Festivals like Le Guess Who? gave her rooms full of people holding still, and DJ Python gave her a beat. Six years passed between albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Because of a Flower · Bandcamp Daily: Because of a Flower
years.h: Kranky debut Because of a Flower takes its name from orchids
years.p: It opens on a spoken passage from W.A. Mathieu's writing and ends on slowed-down piano by the castrato Alessandro Moreschi. Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the title comes from her discovery, at 18, that she is intersex, and from learning that most flowering plants are hermaphroditic; orchids were the symbol used by an online support group. Bandcamp Daily heard "Camille" set against dialogue from a French new-wave film and "Venus" over the sound of water.

Bandcamp Daily gives the release date as November 12; Wikipedia says November 13. It also notes she had already toured supporting Weyes Blood and ran a monthly ambient show on NTS.

years.cap: Ana Roxanne at the Roundhouse, London, c. 2021
years.h: Utrecht books her for Le Guess Who?
years.p: The Quietus ran her festival preview, where she named Deerhoof, Alice Coltrane's Turiya Sings and Deftones' White Pony among her formative records.

years.cap: Ana Roxanne live at KW Studios, Vancouver
years.src: Wikipedia: Natural Wonder Beauty Concept · The Skinny
years.h: Ana Roxanne and [[DJ Python|42343a91-da25-4fb3-aac7-bc297956c79c]] make an album about falling
years.p: Natural Wonder Beauty Concept came out on Mexican Summer, recorded at Gary's Electric Studio in Brooklyn and in home studios in California and New York. Pitchfork gave it 7.4.
years.xp:
Ana Roxanne described the theme to a reviewer as falling: "It's not just falling in love. it's a descent into feeling." Bandcamp picked it as Album of the Day.

The Skinny's review of Poem 1 later called the collaboration one that "managed to neuter both of their respective visions", a minority view against Pitchfork's 7.4.

years.cap: Ana Roxanne live at Silent Green, Berlin
years.p: She played Glastonbury in 2024. The ICA lists her as composer on The Great Animal Orchestra and the feature film First Light.

eras.title: The voice moves to the front
eras.text: Six years after her debut, she dropped the tape loops and layers and released nine songs built around piano, a close microphone and her unprocessed singing.

years.p: The piano ballad was the lead single from Poem 1, with the album date set for May 1 on Kranky.
years.xp: Stereogum ran her Instagram statement: "I can't believe the time has finally come to share this with you, after years of working, ruminating and somehow pushing through to the end."

years.cap: Ana Roxanne in the round at the ICA, London, June 4, 2026
years.src: Metacritic · Arcana.fm · Paste · Stereogum · Twisted Soul Music
years.p: Nine songs on heartbreak and grief, with a muted piano, plucked bass and synthesizers under her plainest singing yet.
years.xp:
Arcana.fm noted she "removed the tape noise, looping and layering" that had dressed her voice before, and Paste heard a microphone so close you can hear her mouth opening and closing. Paste says drums appear for the first time in her work on "Untitled II".

The tracklist includes "Berceuse in A-flat Minor, Op. 45", "One Shall Sleep" and "Wishful (draft)". Metacritic lists Pitchfork at 86 (May 5), Paste at 83 and The Skinny at 80, for a Metascore of 78. Twisted Soul Music says Pitchfork heard 1970s singer-songwriter influence in the sparser songs.
